visuals.heading: MBA Vs No-MBA Entry Routes

items.text: It deserves a real comparison, not a brand-name assumption.
Business analysis gets sold two contradictory ways online.
A requirement almost never arrives clean.
The business analyst's actual job is not writing down what was said.

blocks.heading: Why "Business Analyst" Is Not One Job

items.text: This is the part most generic BA content flattens into one job description.
These four tracks are ordered by real growth headroom, not by how common the entry point is or which one is talked about most.
Banking, insurance, and healthcare follow because domain trust compounds pay quickly inside a regulated sector.

blocks.heading: Questions Before You Commit to This Path

items.text: A salary chart or one relative's opinion about "business analyst scope" cannot tell you whether this fits your specific situation.
Do you feel more energised sitting in a room where three people describe the same problem three different ways, or does that scenario sound exhausting before it even starts.
If a genuinely ambiguous meeting sounds interesting rather than draining, that is a real signal, not a small one.

blocks.heading: Avoid When Deciding on Business Analysis

items.text: "Not coding" is not the same as "easier." The real skill bar here is precision under ambiguity, extracting a clear, buildable requirement from a room of disagreeing stakeholders, which most people are genuinely bad at by default and cannot fake for long.
IT-services BA work rotates you across client accounts fast, which builds breadth early.

visuals.heading: Will AI Replace Business Analysts

items.text: First-draft business requirement documents from a recorded stakeholder meeting, using transcription and summarisation tools now built into Confluence, Notion, and dedicated meeting-notes apps.
Turning a rough requirement into a first-pass set of user stories with draft acceptance criteria, cutting the blank-page time on routine, well-understood requests.
Generating a first current-state process map from a described workflow, which used to be a slow manual diagramming task.

blocks.heading: Not a Flat Yes or No

items.text: You get real energy from resolving disagreement and structuring an ambiguous problem, not just documenting a clear one.
You have honestly weighed the MBA-vs-no-MBA cost and speed trade-off against your own runway, not just picked the option that sounds more prestigious.
You are willing to build domain depth in one sector (banking, insurance, healthcare, or IT-services breadth) rather than treating "business analyst" as one interchangeable generic title.
You are open to the BA-to-product-manager bridge later, on purpose, rather than assuming the title alone will carry you there.
